findings.title: Stale month after dismiss or selection
findings.message: Month navigation sets p.month but nothing re-renders explicitly from the callbacks, and the calendar popover's month is reset on every toggle. More importantly, after selecting a day, p.month is not reset, so reopening later by Dismiss (which only sets calendarOpen=false) can show a stale navigated month instead of the Value's month.
findings.suggestion: Reset p.month = time.Time{} in Dismiss and after day selection.

findings.title: Strict textual round-trip rejects valid input
findings.message: The round-trip check compares a formatted value against trimmed input. Layouts with non-padded or case-variant elements (e.g. 'Jan' vs 'jan', or '3:04 PM' accepting 'pm') or where TimeOnly drops fields will reject valid user input. Layouts like '2006-1-2' also reject '2024-02-29'. Users typing legitimate variants get Invalid errors.
findings.suggestion: Detect DST normalization by comparing the hour/minute of v to parsed instead of requiring textual equality.

finding.title: Location pointer comparison is fragile
finding.message: The available() closure compares *time.Location pointers with ==. A time.Time whose location is UTC may carry a nil loc pointer in some forms, and Local vs UTC pointer identity can differ between values returned by Date/Format paths; any Change callback setting Value to a time with an equivalent but differently-pointed location will mark the picker unavailable and silently drop edits.
finding.suggestion: Compare location by name (p.Value.Location().String() == location.String()) or drop the location check, since the callback itself would normally preserve the location.
